cases.name: unterminated_frame_is_discarded
cases.why: a frame with no trailing newline is never dispatched: ReadString returns it together with io.EOF and the loop returns on EOF first. The client gets silence, not an error

cases.name: unterminated_frame_after_complete_frame
cases.why: the terminated frame is answered and the unterminated remainder is dropped, so a client that forgets the last newline loses exactly one request
cases.stdout_raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{}}

cases.name: crlf_line_ending
cases.why: a CRLF client works: the carriage return stays on the line and the JSON decoder skips it as trailing whitespace
cases.stdout_raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{}}

cases.name: leading_whitespace
cases.why: leading whitespace before the frame is tolerated by the decoder
cases.stdout_raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{}}

cases.name: trailing_whitespace
cases.why: trailing whitespace after the frame is tolerated by the decoder
cases.stdout_raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{}}

cases.name: nul_byte_in_frame
cases.why: an embedded NUL is a decode failure, answered as -32700 rather than crashing the reader
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"invalid character '\\x00' looking for beginning of value","message":"Parse error","code":-32700},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}

cases.name: two_objects_on_one_line
cases.why: frames are newline-delimited, not self-delimiting: a second object on the same line is trailing garbage
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"invalid character '{' after top-level value","message":"Parse error","code":-32700},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}

cases.name: array_frame
cases.why: a non-object top-level frame is -32700, not a crash
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type transport.Message","message":"Parse error","code":-32700},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}

cases.name: bare_string_frame
cases.why: a bare JSON string is -32700
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type transport.Message","message":"Parse error","code":-32700},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}

cases.name: null_frame
cases.why: literal null decodes to a zero-valued message whose jsonrpc is empty, so it is -32600 and not -32700
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"jsonrpc must be 2.0","message":"Invalid Request","code":-32600},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}

cases.name: only_newlines
cases.why: each blank line is its own parse error; three blank lines produce three frames

cases.name: empty_stream
cases.why: an empty stream writes nothing and shuts down cleanly

cases.name: unicode_method_name
cases.why: a non-ASCII method name round-trips into the not-found message without escaping
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"message":"Method not found: pïng✓","code":-32601},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}

cases.name: bignum_id_preserved_verbatim
cases.why: an ID far beyond int64 is echoed back byte-for-byte because it is never decoded into a number

cases.name: duplicate_key_inside_params
cases.why: ADR 0034 item 15: a plain duplicate key inside params (not the envelope) is last-wins in encoding/json, so initialize negotiates the SECOND protocolVersion (2025-03-26) although 2024-11-05 came first. The port is last-wins as well, so this is parity and not a divergence; only duplicated ENVELOPE keys are rejected (see the divergences). The wrong-typed-duplicate shapes below are where encoding/json fails the whole decode

cases.name: duplicate_params_wrong_typed_first
cases.why: MCP-004-DUP: protocolVersion 123 then a valid string. encoding/json records the first UnmarshalTypeError and returns it even though a later valid member follows, so this is -32602 and not a negotiated 2025-03-26
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"json: cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field InitializeParams.protocolVersion of type string","message":"Invalid params","code":-32602},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}

cases.name: duplicate_params_wrong_typed_last
cases.why: a valid protocolVersion followed by a wrong-typed duplicate is -32602 as well: the error does not depend on which duplicate is last
cases.stdout_raw: {"error":{"data":"json: cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field InitializeParams.protocolVersion of type string","message":"Invalid params","code":-32602},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}

cases.name: duplicate_params_null_after_string_keeps_string
cases.why: null is a no-op against a string target, so a trailing protocolVersion:null does NOT reset an earlier real version: 2024-11-05 is negotiated, where a naive last-wins would negotiate the latest version

cases.name: interleaved_valid_and_invalid
cases.why: a hostile client cannot desynchronise the stream: every frame is answered in order regardless of the failures between them

bounds.name: oversized_five_megabyte_frame
bounds.why: input is NOT bounded: the oracle's reader grows without limit and answers a five-megabyte frame normally. The row's 'bounded input' wording describes an intent the oracle does not implement

bounds.name: brackets_inside_a_string_are_not_nesting
bounds.why: a payload of bracket CHARACTERS inside a string literal is depth 1, not deep nesting. The oracle dispatches it, so a depth guard that scans without tracking string state would reject a frame the oracle accepts

bounds.name: escaped_quote_before_bracket_fill_is_still_a_string
bounds.why: the depth scanner has to track backslash escapes, not just quotes: after an escaped quote the scanner is STILL inside the string, so these brackets are characters and the frame is dispatched. A scanner that treated the escaped quote as closing the string would count them as nesting and wrongly reject

divergences.name: duplicate_object_keys_last_wins
divergences.oracle_behavior: The oracle accepts a frame carrying the id key twice and answers with the LAST occurrence, silently: encoding/json resolves duplicates by last-wins. Verified by executing it in this generator, which fails if it stops reproducing. SCOPE: this covers duplicated ENVELOPE fields only. A plain duplicate key INSIDE params is last-wins in both the oracle and the port (cases duplicate_key_inside_params and duplicate_params_*), and a wrong-typed earlier duplicate there fails the decode with -32602 in both, as encoding/json does; neither is a divergence. A duplicate inside an id or an unknown top-level key is also accepted last-wins exactly as the oracle does, because those are carried as raw values and never decoded into a struct. NOT covered here: tools/call. Go keeps arguments as a json.RawMessage; Rust re-parses them as a serde_json::Value (last-wins per object like encoding/json into a map, but duplicate-key fidelity INSIDE arguments is untested), and a Value nests at most 128 levels where Go accepts up to 10000, so deeper arguments are -32602 in Rust (declared in ADR 0034 item 15). tools/call is not exercised by this fixture at all: the oracle answers 'vault locked' before it decodes params when no tool runtime is attached.
divergences.rust_behavior: Rust answers -32700 and does not dispatch the frame.
divergences.rationale: serde rejects duplicate struct fields and the adjudication keeps that rather than relaxing it to match. Last-wins is the classic duplicate-key smuggling shape: an intermediary that logs, audits or applies policy to a frame reads the first occurrence while the server acts on the last, so the two disagree about what was requested. SymVault has exactly such a policy and audit layer, which makes this security-relevant rather than cosmetic. Rejecting is the stricter side, and the migration contract names duplicate keys as a case to decide deliberately rather than inherit. Recorded, not silent; reversing it is a coordinator decision.

divergences.name: invalid_utf8_id_echoed_verbatim
divergences.oracle_behavior: The oracle accepts a frame whose id contains invalid UTF-8 and echoes those bytes back on stdout unchanged, because json.RawMessage is []byte and Go strings are not required to be valid UTF-8. Verified by executing it in this generator, which fails if it stops reproducing.
divergences.oracle_stdout_note: not embedded: the byte sequence is not valid UTF-8 and so cannot be carried in this JSON fixture
divergences.rust_behavior: Rust answers -32700 and emits no invalid bytes.
divergences.rationale: serde_json's RawValue is backed by str and cannot hold invalid UTF-8, so byte-verbatim echo is not reachable without replacing the JSON envelope wholesale. The adjudicated behavior is to reject fail-closed, which is also the stricter of the two: the oracle's behavior puts attacker-chosen invalid bytes onto the same stdout stream the client parses as framing. This is a deliberate, recorded divergence and not a silent one; reversing it is a coordinator decision.
